metadata.author: timchen
metadata.question: How much of the measured ranking quality is attributable to generative AI, as opposed to the reviewed seed ontology and behavior aggregates?
why_this_is_not_release_evidence: 499 evaluation queries; both locked confirmations use 1,991 and 1,992.
The ranking model was trained on 1,673 groups; the locked run used 39,335 (4.3%).
The test window [2400,2600) is a subset of the already-consumed confirmation window [2400,3400), so it cannot support a fresh claim.
Every paired bootstrap confidence interval crosses zero.
Bedrock node coverage comes from a bounded 200-record pilot, not the full train-only corpus.

jd_skill_extraction.note: Reused the frozen pilot output already committed in artifacts/demo-index.json.

bedrock_node_family.design: same trained model; only the Bedrock-derived llm_* feature family zeroed at inference
bedrock_node_family.verdict: positive point estimate, confidence interval crosses zero by 0.0002; not significant at this sample size

query_normalization.design: one fixed model scoring two feature sets; only the resolved-skill surface differs

sanity_check.note: A query the LLM did not rewrite must score identically. This gate confirms the comparison is not contaminated by model retraining.

coverage.note: 45 hand-written nodes reach 9x more queries than 882 Bedrock nodes, because the seed ontology was authored around search vocabulary while extraction produces job-description vocabulary.

reranking_ceiling.statement: The offline benchmark reranks the original exposure list, so any improvement that would surface a job the previous system never showed is unmeasurable by construction.
reasons_ndcg_did_not_improve: already saturated: the single relevant job was ranked first before the change
signal landed only on non-relevant candidates, reordering them without moving a relevant job
relevant job moved but stayed inside the same effective rank band
signal was uniform across all candidates, so relative order could not change

downstream_dependency.statement: Query-side normalization is capped by job-side edge coverage. Rewrites resolved the correct occupation node in every inspected case, but only 37.5% of relevant candidates carried a matching edge, so the signal became noise as often as evidence.
downstream_dependency.implication: Scaling train-only JD extraction is a prerequisite for measuring query normalization, not an independent alternative.

methodological_correction.statement: An earlier version of this comparison trained a second model on the rewritten pairs and reported -0.98% for query normalization. That number was model-retraining variance, not rewrite effect: 356 unrewritten queries also moved, 106 worse and 112 better. Holding the model fixed reduced the effect to -0.06%.
methodological_correction.retained_because: the failure mode is easy to repeat and the discarded number should not resurface as evidence

online_configuration_risk.statement: Query normalization runs synchronously on every search request with a 2.0 second read timeout. Measured p95 was 2094.6 ms, so more than 5% of live requests would fall back to deterministic normalization and report a degraded component.
online_configuration_risk.second_risk: One Bedrock call per request exceeds the event's 1 request-per-second ceiling under any sustained judge traffic.

next_steps: Run train-only JD extraction across the 22,674 graph-eligible judged candidates to lift job-side edge coverage above 6.5%.
Resolve duplicate canonical nodes before scaling: the pilot emitted Microsoft Excel (37) and Excel (34) as separate nodes.
Serialize pipeline/bedrock_extract.py to one request per second; --max-workers currently defaults to 4.
Change the pipeline/bedrock_extract.py default region from ap-northeast-1, which is outside the permitted deployment regions.
Re-measure both arms on the untouched [4400,5400) window with full-scale training before any release claim.
